name: Fig Puddings
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: good dried figs
ingredients.originalText: half a pound of good dried figs

ingredients.name: fine, dry bread crumbs
ingredients.originalText: two cupfuls of fine, dry bread crumbs

ingredients.name: beef suet, powdered
ingredients.originalText: half a cupful of beef suet, powdered

ingredients.name: scant cupfuls of sweet milk
ingredients.originalText: two scant cupfuls of sweet milk

ingredients.name: white sugar
ingredients.originalText: half a cupful of white sugar

ingredients.name: baking powder

ingredients.name: sifted flour
ingredients.originalText: half a cupful of sifted flour

instructions.text: Wash, wipe and mince the figs
Soak the crumbs in milk, add the eggs, beaten light, with sugar, salt, suet, flour and figs
Put in buttered molds with tight top, set in boiling water with weight on cover to prevent mold from upsetting
Eat hot with hard sauce or butter, powdered sugar, one teaspoonful of extract of nutmeg

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Wash, wipe and mince the figs
2. Soak the crumbs in milk, add the eggs, beaten light, with sugar, salt, suet, flour and figs
3. Beat three minutes
4. Put in buttered molds with tight top, set in boiling water with weight on cover to prevent mold from upsetting
5. Boil three hours
6. Eat hot with hard sauce or butter, powdered sugar, one teaspoonful of extract of nutmeg
